data.body_html:
When it comes to marbella snorkeling spots cabopino estepona, you have two very different underwater worlds within easy reach of Puerto Banús. Cabopino, to the east, offers calm, shallow coves perfect for beginners and families. Estepona, to the west, delivers rocky reefs and deeper drops that reward more experienced snorkelers. Both are accessible by private boat charter, and the right choice depends on your group's skill level and what you want to see beneath the surface. Here's how they compare, with concrete distances, depths, and rental options.

Cabopino: The Family-Friendly Choice

Cabopino sits about 8 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús, a 30-minute cruise at 16 knots. The area is known for its sandy coves and shallow seagrass meadows, where the water depth rarely exceeds 6 meters. This makes it ideal for children and less confident swimmers. The seabed is a mix of fine sand and posidonia seagrass, home to seabream, damselfish, and the occasional octopus tucked into rocky crevices.

Visibility in Cabopino typically ranges from 5 to 10 meters, depending on wind and recent rainfall. The sheltered coves mean minimal current, so you can float and observe without fighting the water. For a relaxed half-day trip, a 2-hour charter on our Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (€749/2h) gives you just enough time to anchor, snorkel, and enjoy a drink on board.

Estepona: The Adventurer's Reef

Estepona lies 12 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús, about 45 minutes at 16 knots. The underwater terrain here is more dramatic: rocky reefs, underwater cliffs, and drop-offs that plunge to 15-20 meters. This attracts a richer diversity of marine life, including groupers, moray eels, and occasionally rays gliding over the sand. Visibility is often better than Cabopino, reaching 10-20 meters on calm days.

However, Estepona's reefs can have stronger currents, especially around the headlands. This is not a spot for novices. If you're an experienced snorkeler or diver, you'll appreciate the challenge and the rewards. Because of the distance, a 2-hour charter won't work—you'll need at least 4 hours. Our Mangusta 80 (from €4,719/4h) includes a free jet ski, letting you zip between reefs and find the best calm-water spots.

Water Clarity and Temperature: A Seasonal Guide

Both locations share the same Mediterranean water, but local geography affects clarity. Cabopino's sandy bottom and shallower depth can stir up sediment after storms, reducing visibility. Estepona's rocky reefs tend to keep water clearer, but upwellings can bring cooler, nutrient-rich water that attracts fish.

For the best experience, book between June and September. If you're sensitive to cold, ask about wetsuit rental (not included in standard charters).

Boat Options for Your Snorkeling Trip

Your choice of boat affects how quickly you reach the snorkeling grounds and how comfortable you are between dips. Here's a quick guide to our fleet:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – €749/2h, perfect for Cabopino.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – same price, slightly larger capacity.
  • Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) – faster, reaches Estepona in ~40 min.
  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) – spacious deck for gear.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – from €4,719/4h, includes jet ski.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs.

How to Plan Your Day: Itinerary Ideas

For a morning trip to Cabopino, depart Puerto Banús at 9:00, anchor by 9:30, snorkel for 1.5 hours, then enjoy a light lunch on board before returning by 11:30. For Estepona, depart at 8:30 to catch calm seas, snorkel at two different reefs, and return by 13:00. If you want both, book a full-day charter (8 hours) and plan to cruise between the two—about 1.5 hours each way.

Remember to bring reef-safe sunscreen, a rash guard, and an underwater camera. The skipper can drop anchor in sheltered spots, but always check conditions on the day.

Safety and Regulations

All our skippers are licensed and brief you on safety before departure. Life jackets are available for all passengers, and snorkeling is only permitted in designated areas. Avoid touching marine life or standing on seagrass beds—they're protected. If you're unsure about currents, ask the skipper for advice; they know the local conditions intimately.

Why Choose a Private Charter Over a Group Tour?

A private charter gives you the flexibility to choose your snorkeling spot, set your own pace, and avoid crowded beaches. You're not tied to a group schedule, and you can request specific stops like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. For the same price as a group tour, you get exclusivity and a skipper who knows the best hidden coves.
